analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: The Franco-German 10yr spread widened +32bps last week to 141bps, the biggest weekly widening in Bloomberg data back to 1990. It hit +160bps intraday on Friday before the weak US payroll print helped reverse the move.

DB's view is that the French selloff is mostly a positioning flush, not new fundamentals. An aggressive ECB hiking cycle was priced into a market where leveraged investors held French front-end carry. Large VAR swings in OATs forced those positions out and the move became disorderly.

DB rates sees OATs as around 40-50bps cheap even relative to France's weak fundamentals, which implies a large political-risk premium is embedded in prices. DB strategists are not yet comfortable buying OATs outright.

Higher French yields are tightening financial conditions and should make it harder for the ECB to deliver the hikes priced. DB economists see the ECB terminal rate nearer 2.75%, perhaps 3%, versus 3.5% priced 8 business days ago and 3.20% now. The ECB terminal rate fell to 3.01% at Friday's weakest point.

DB sees the French budget as more likely to pass than in the last two years, RN as trying to build fiscal credibility, and French banks as having much less sovereign-bank feedback risk than earlier peripheral crises. Its path case is that things get worse before they get better, with the selloff itself pushing politicians and European institutions toward a solution.
The euro is down 0.72% this morning while European and US equity futures are flat. There is talk the Spanish government may call an early election after losing two housing bills on Friday.

Brazil's first round surprised: Flávio Bolsonaro took about 47.0% of valid votes against about 45.1% for Lula, with a run-off on October 25. Right-leaning parties raised their Senate seat share from 47% to 63%.

DB LatAm rates strategists expect a broad rally of around 100bp in Brazilian DI rates as the election premium unwinds, and favour front-end receivers. Brazil equity ETFs traded up as much as 10% in Asia.

US September payrolls rose +29k against +133k expected. Private payrolls were +46k versus +127k expected, revisions were -60k over the prior two months, and average hourly earnings rose +0.1% versus +0.3% expected.

DB US economists read the labour details as broadly stable. Unemployment rose to 4.175% from 4.141%, U-6 fell to 7.6%, and participation rose to 61.8%. They still expect two more 25bp Fed hikes over the next couple of quarters.

Markets price another 86bps of Fed hikes over the next 12 months, down from 100bps early last week and up from 70bps just after the payroll release. The chance of an October Fed hike fell from 64% to 23% over the week and the ECB October hike from 42% to 14%.
The 10yr Treasury yield rose +11bps last week to 5.27%, a fifth straight weekly rise. It traded as low as 5.155% just after payrolls on Friday.

Italy's 10yr spread over bunds widened +23bps to 114bps, the biggest weekly rise since April 2020. The 10yr bund yield fell -14.0bps to 3.46%, its biggest weekly decline since the Liberation Day tariff week in April 2025.
Euro IG spreads widened +14bps and HY +47bps last week, the biggest weekly jump since the post-Liberation Day selloff in April. US IG widened +2bps and HY +12bps.
Brent rose +4.94% last week to $102.25/bbl (December contract). European diesel fell -7.31% after the G7 announced a plan to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel reserves.

The S&P 500 fell only -0.27% on the week despite large swings, including a +0.73% jump on Friday after the jobs report. The week ahead centres on the FOMC minutes (Wed), the ECB account (Thu), US ISM services (today) and the University of Michigan survey (Fri).
Japan's September services PMI fell to 51.3 from 52.5 in August, below expectations. The Nikkei is up +2.53% led by technology.
earnings_insights: Earnings this week per the DB calendar: Applied Digital (Wed Oct 7), PepsiCo, Fast Retailing and Tesco (Thu Oct 8), Delta Air Lines (Fri Oct 9). No estimates or guidance are given.

tension_points.bull_case: The move is a positioning flush, not new fundamentals. OATs are 40-50bps cheap even versus weak fundamentals, the French budget is more likely to pass, RN is courting fiscal credibility, and French banks carry less sovereign feedback risk. DB's bias is that markets have overshot.
tension_points.bear_case: The fiscal problem is real and has built for years, and DB says the lows in French assets are not necessarily in. Contagion could worsen before it improves, and DB strategists are not yet comfortable buying OATs outright.

tension_points.theme: Fed hike path after weak payrolls
tension_points.bull_case: The labour market is broadly stable (unemployment 4.175%, U-6 down to 7.6%, participation 61.8%), so DB economists still expect two more 25bp Fed hikes over the next couple of quarters.
tension_points.bear_case: Headline payrolls missed badly (+29k vs +133k) with 60k of downward revisions and weak wages, and the October hike chance fell from 64% to 23%. Jefferson and Williams prefer to wait for more data.
